extracted.intended_audience: researchers and reviewers conducting critical appraisal of qualitative studies (e.g., systematic reviewers, health services researchers, journal peer reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Apply the CASP (Critical Appraisal Skills Programme) qualitative checklist to evaluate the quality, rigour, and value of individual qualitative research studies, using 10 core questions with supporting prompts to summarise strengths and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Was there a clear statement of the aims of the research?
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim can be determined from anywhere in the paper (e.g. title, abstract, introduction, methods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the research aims/questions are explicitly stated and identifiable anywhere in the report (title, abstract, introduction, methods). Main item scored 'yes', 'no' or 'unclear'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is a qualitative methodology appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualitative research is the appropriate way to address the aim or answer the research question (e.g. the research concerns experiences/views of participants, processes involved, or the nature of interactions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the topic and aims justify qualitative methods (e.g., exploring experiences, meanings, processes). Consider mismatch between question and methodology; score 'yes', 'no' or 'unclear'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Was the research design appropriate to address the aims of the research?
rubrics_metrics.description: Data collection, data analysis and methodological approach are appropriate to address the aim or answer the research question; the review team classified methodological approach based on whether the approach had consistently been used throughout (e.g. grounded theory required analytical methods such as constant comparison as well as the development of a core category or theory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether chosen design (e.g., grounded theory, phenomenology, ethnography) and its application are coherent and consistently applied across data collection and analysis. Look for evidence the approach was followed throughout. Score 'yes', 'no' or 'unclear'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Was the recruitment strategy appropriate to the aims of the research?
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors clearly report selection of participants and this is appropriate to address the aim or answer the research question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that participant selection/sampling strategy is described and justified relative to the research aims. Additional prompt: Is the sampling method clearly described? Use prompts to summarise strengths/limitations; score 'yes', 'no' or 'unclear'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Was the data collected in a way that addressed the research issue?
rubrics_metrics.description: Type of data collection method is clear (e.g. interview, focus group, participant observation, online postings) and has potential to address the aim or research question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether data collection methods are appropriate and adequately described. Additional prompt: Is the method of data collection clearly described? Assess potential for methods to elicit data relevant to aims; score 'yes', 'no' or 'unclear'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Has the relationship between researcher and participants been adequately considered?
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors demonstrate self-reflexivity in data collection and data analysis processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for reflexivity statements addressing researcher influence, positionality, and the researcher–participant relationship and how these were managed in collection and analysis. Score 'yes', 'no' or 'unclear'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have ethical issues been taken into consideration?
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval from an ethics committee is reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for statements about ethical approval, consent procedures, confidentiality, and other ethical considerations. Presence or absence of ethics reporting informs the 'yes'/'no'/'unclear' judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Was the data analysis sufficiently rigorous?
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors clearly describe data analysis approach and employ strategies to ensure rigour (e.g. peer debriefing, member checking, negative cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity and appropriateness of analytic methods and use of strategies to enhance rigour (peer debriefing, member checking, seeking negative cases, audit trails). Additional prompts: Is the method of analysis clearly described? Are the claims made supported by sufficient evidence? Are sufficient data presented to support the descriptive findings? Are you confident that all of the data were taken into account? Use these prompts to inform the 'yes'/'no'/'unclear' score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is there a clear statement of findings?
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings are clearly stated (e.g. in the abstract or findings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether findings are presented clearly and logically, with appropriate distinction between data and interpretation; consider whether findings are summarized in abstract and findings sections. Score 'yes', 'no' or 'unclear'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the research valuable?
rubrics_metrics.description: Study appears valuable in own right (i.e. something has been ‘learnt’), rather than judged in relation to contribution made to the current review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the study's contribution: Does the study add to knowledge or theory in the field? Does the study demonstrate theoretical insight, novel findings or perspectives? Use these prompts to summarise value; main item scored 'yes', 'no' or 'unclear'. Note: the main 10 items are scored 'yes'/'no'/'unclear' while additional prompts are used to facilitate summarising main strengths, limitations and concerns of each study.
